extendedContent.title: Origins & Mythology
extendedContent.content: The myth of Dangun is primarily found in the Samguk Yusa (Memorabilia of the Three Kingdoms), written in the 13th century. It recounts how Hwanung, son of Hwanin (the Lord of Heaven), descended to Mount Taebaek with three thousand followers. He established Sinsi (神市), a city where he taught humans agriculture, medicine, and governance. A bear and a tiger sought to become human. Hwanung gave them mugwort and garlic, instructing them to eat only this sacred food and avoid sunlight for 100 days. The tiger failed, but the bear persevered, transforming into a woman named Ungnyeo (熊女). Ungnyeo then prayed to conceive a child. Hwanung, moved by her devotion, transformed himself and married Ungnyeo, who gave birth to Dangun Wanggeom (檀君王儉). Dangun established Gojoseon, which marked the start of the Korean nation, and ruled for 1,500 years before abdicating and becoming a mountain god.

extendedContent.title: Role & Significance
extendedContent.content: Dangun holds immense cultural and national significance in Korea. He is revered as the progenitor of the Korean people and the founder of the first Korean kingdom, Gojoseon. His myth legitimizes Korean national identity and provides a sense of shared ancestry and cultural heritage. Dangun's story emphasizes the importance of perseverance, the connection between humans and nature (represented by the bear), and the divine mandate to rule. The myth also highlights the importance of agriculture and civilization, as Hwanung taught these skills to humans. Dangun's legacy is deeply embedded in Korean patriotism and national pride. He is a symbol of Korean independence and cultural distinctiveness.

extendedContent.title: Symbolism & Interpretation
extendedContent.content: The Dangun myth is rich in symbolism. The bear represents the primitive, natural world and the potential for transformation and enlightenment through perseverance. The tiger, in contrast, symbolizes impatience and the inability to overcome challenges. The mugwort and garlic symbolize the trials and sacrifices necessary for achieving a higher state of being. Hwanung represents divine intervention and the guidance necessary for civilization to flourish. Dangun himself symbolizes the ideal ruler, embodying wisdom, strength, and a connection to both the divine and the human realms. The myth can be interpreted as an allegory for the development of civilization, the taming of nature, and the establishment of a just and prosperous society. The mountainous setting is also significant, reflecting the importance of mountains in Korean culture and spirituality.

extendedContent.title: Legacy & Influence
extendedContent.content: Dangun's legacy continues to resonate in modern Korea. His birthday, October 3rd (Gaecheonjeol, or National Foundation Day), is a national holiday. Dangun is often invoked in patriotic and nationalistic rhetoric. Statues and monuments dedicated to Dangun can be found throughout Korea. His story is taught in schools, reinforcing his role as the father of the Korean nation. The myth of Dangun has also influenced Korean art, literature, and popular culture. He remains a potent symbol of Korean identity and a source of national pride. Even in the face of modernization and globalization, Dangun's story continues to provide a sense of continuity and connection to the past.

role: Founder and divine ancestor of the Korean people
description: Dangun is the legendary founder and first king of Gojoseon, considered the first Korean kingdom. According to the Samguk Yusa, a collection of Korean legends and history, Hwanung, son of the Lord of Heaven Hwanin, descended to Earth and desired to rule humans. He established a city and taught humans various arts and laws. A bear and a tiger prayed to Hwanung to become human. Hwanung gave them sacred mugwort and garlic and instructed them to avoid sunlight. The tiger failed, but the bear persevered and transformed into a woman named Ungnyeo. Ungnyeo prayed for a child and Hwanung took her as his wife, and she gave birth to Dangun. Dangun established Gojoseon and ruled for many years before becoming a mountain god.
